founders.background: Studied Electrical Engineering and Computer Science at UC Berkeley. Spent 5 years at Robinhood as a Senior PM and then Group PM for Customer Care, building 24/7 customer support and back-office dispute operations for 20 million members. Previously worked at Meta, where he met co-founder Saisi Peters.
founders.notable_achievement: Selected for Inc.'s 'Female Founders 500'. Her experience designing dispute operations at a large fintech became the starting point for product design.

founders.background: At Chime, as a Product Manager responsible for back-office operations automation, she built an in-house dispute management system that saved approximately $10M in operational losses in its first year (per media reports). Worked with Shanthi Shanmugam at Meta. Also listed as 'Saisi Peter' on Crunchbase.
founders.notable_achievement: Productized the problem definition that unresolved disputes are the second leading cause of customer churn at digital banks.

casap-2026.team_highlights: Both founders come from hands-on roles at large fintechs (Robinhood and Chime) where they built and automated dispute and customer support operations. In February 2025, Casap was selected as a strategic alliance provider for CUNA Strategic Services (CSS) under the American Credit Union Association, entering the community credit union channel. They operate a 'forward-deployed' team that embeds with clients to redesign workflows. The organization size is undisclosed (estimated 51-100 people).

product.summary: A platform for financial institutions that uses AI agents to handle card payment disputes, chargebacks, and first-party fraud. It covers the entire lifecycle: intake, investigation, decision-making, evidence collection, chargeback, and consumer communication. In October 2026, with a funding round, they announced expanding scope from disputes and fraud to collections, claims, and complex exceptions.
product.problem_statement: Consumer protection regulations such as Reg E and Reg Z impose deadlines on banks for dispute resolution, while first-party fraud (where a consumer denies a legitimate charge on their own card) is growing at 2.5x per year, pushing manual investigation to its limits. The CEO explains that due to investigation costs, disputes under about $30 are often resolved in the customer's favor without investigation.
product.solution: Specialized AI agents that learn each institution's policies and procedures operate on top of existing core and digital banking systems to investigate, decide, and take action. All decisions are accompanied by rationale and action history, ensuring explainability and auditability. Cases requiring judgment are escalated to humans.
key_features: Dispute AI Agent: Analyzes transaction context, user history, merchant reputation, etc., to automatically decide on provisional credits, chargeback filings, or rejections.
Dynamic Intake: The company explains that it filters out up to 30% of invalid disputes at the intake stage, such as those caused by billing statement confusion.
First-Party Fraud Score: A score trained on anonymized cross-institution dispute data to proactively identify habitual refund abuse (described by the company as a 'FICO for first-party fraud').

Embedded Regulatory and Card Network Rules: Automatically applies Reg E, Reg Z, Nacha, Visa and Mastercard submission regulations, generating chargeback documents that meet deadlines and evidence requirements.
API Integration and Exception Handling: Integrates with core systems, digital channels, and card networks, with expansion into adjacent areas like collections and claims.
product.tech_stack_or_innovation: The company states that it combines proprietary specialized models with several large foundation models to create a decision-making system for dispute processing. The differentiation lies not in the models themselves but in embedding regulatory and card network rules as code in the product's foundation, and in the first-party fraud signals derived from anonymized cross-institution dispute data. The exact composition of models and stack is not disclosed.
product.target_customer: US retail banks, community credit unions, fintech card issuers, and payment processors. The company reports over 100 institutions are using it, and the credit union channel is addressed through the CUNA Strategic Services partnership.
product.business_model: Appears to be an enterprise SaaS licensing model for financial institutions, combined with implementation and operational support from the forward-deployed team (est.). Contract pricing and billing units are not disclosed.

direct_competitors.comparison: A larger dispute and fraud workflow specialist in terms of capital and scale. Strong in enterprise workflows, but relatively less focused on using generative AI for intake questioning and proactive first-party fraud defense.
Team is strong but customer base is skewed toward young fintech card issuers; in community bank and credit union references, Casap is described as ahead.
A tool focused on regulatory deadline compliance; relatively weaker in end-to-end investigation including chargeback tracking and recovery with card networks.
Similarly strong in regulatory deadline management, but differs in the dimension of first-party fraud scoring and investigation automation.

A player that helps merchants prevent payment fraud or respond to chargebacks from the merchant side, standing on the opposite side of the transaction from Casap, which automates issuer-side dispute operations.

competitive_landscape.key_differentiator: End-to-end automation of issuer-side dispute operations, with a core emphasis on a first-party fraud score based on anonymized cross-institution data. This is combined with embedded regulatory and card rules and a distribution advantage through the credit union channel (CSS partnership).
competitive_landscape.moat: First, the first-party fraud signals from anonymized cross-institution dispute data create a data network effect that strengthens as customer count grows. Second, regulatory engineering that embeds Reg E, Reg Z, Nacha, Visa/Mastercard rules into the product's foundation, enabling auditability. Third, the credit union distribution network secured through CUNA Strategic Services strategic provider status. Fourth, a forward-deployed organization that embeds with clients to redesign workflows.
competitive_landscape.competitive_position_summary: Issuer-side dispute automation has historically attracted less capital than merchant-side. Incumbents like Quavo and newer specialized players like Decisionly, FINBOA, and Mightybot coexist. Casap is pursuing a path of first securing 100 institutions in a narrow market with three axes—first-party fraud score + embedded regulation + credit union channel—and then expanding into collections and claims with the same customers.

general-compute-2026.tagline: An inference neocloud built on inference ASICs instead of NVIDIA GPUs

founders.background: Public information about his background before founding is limited. He is known to have led hardware financing and capital structure design.
founders.notable_achievement: Raised a $15M seed in May 2026, a $100M Series A in October, and a $400M hardware financing facility from Upper90 in quick succession.

founders.background: Oversaw technical architecture and published a public analysis of NVIDIA GPU bottlenecks in decoding large models.
founders.notable_achievement: Designed a prefill/decode disaggregation stack, including adoption of Cerebras wafer-scale inference, and led vendor partnerships.

general-compute-2026.team_highlights: Beyond the two co-founders, team size is undisclosed. It already operates 30MW+ of capacity and will begin running Cerebras-based agentic coding workloads in Q1 2027.

product.summary: General Compute is an inference-only cloud that pairs NVIDIA GPUs with inference-specific ASICs from Cerebras, SambaNova, Positron, and others. It buys chips directly, deploys them in existing U.S. colocation data centers, and sells dedicated inference capacity to customers as bare metal or through a single API.
product.problem_statement: For large language model decoding, memory bandwidth bottlenecks make GPUs inefficient. Existing neoclouds built around NVIDIA GPUs are facing growing skepticism about whether they can be profitable amid an intense race for capital and power.
product.solution: It lowers per-token cost with a disaggregated inference architecture: prefill on NVIDIA GPUs, decode on inference-specific ASICs. General Compute owns the hardware assets, and customers get dedicated inference capacity through one contract and one SLA.
key_features: Offered on a bare-metal or TPS SLA basis with no separate software layer
Configured and deployed with chip-specific power, cooling, networking, and software
NVIDIA GPU prefill + Cerebras, SambaNova, Positron, and d-Matrix decode configuration
Access to multiple chip architectures via a single API and a single contract
Uses existing U.S. colocation and former Bitcoin mining sites for power and facility capacity
product.tech_stack_or_innovation: A disaggregation stack that splits each request into prefill and decode and processes them on different chips. It is distinctive for building the fleet based on actual customer demand rather than demand from chip suppliers.
product.target_customer: Cloud companies that provide high-speed inference to developers (e.g., Baseten), companies running agentic coding workloads, and LLM services that need low-latency token streaming.
product.business_model: An asset-heavy neocloud. Hardware purchases are financed through Upper90's debt facility, operating capital is raised through equity, and revenue comes from selling inference tokens and dedicated capacity.

direct_competitors.comparison: A GPU-based inference cloud. General Compute claims 2.6x faster TTFT and 4.6x faster end-to-end latency on the GPT-OSS-120B benchmark.

direct_competitors.comparison: A model that builds large-scale data centers with NVIDIA GPUs. General Compute's strategy is to place heterogeneous chips in existing colocation facilities instead of building hyperscale data centers, reducing capital and power burdens.

competitive_landscape.key_differentiator: A disaggregated inference architecture that separates requests into prefill (NVIDIA) and decode (ASIC), plus an asset-heavy model that acts as an alternative distribution channel for chip vendors.
competitive_landscape.moat: Multi-year supply agreements with Cerebras and others, a commercial workload reference based on SambaNova SN40L, a $400M hardware financing facility, and over 30MW of secured capacity. Economies of scale are still limited.

founders.background: PhD. Former CEO of Enthera (raised Italy's largest biotech Series A) and CSO of ADIENNE. Experienced with U.S. FDA approval of thiotepa.
founders.notable_achievement: Raised the largest seed investment in European biotech history (€40M)

founders.background: MD, PhD. 15+ years of research in RNA biology and DNA methylation. Lead author in Nature and Nature Communications. Co-founded SpeaRNA.
founders.notable_achievement: Led the key discovery of DiRs (DNMTs Interacting RNAs)

founders.background: Professor at Harvard Medical School, Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center. World authority on blood cancer and RNA transcriptional regulation.
founders.notable_achievement: Leads the lab where DiRs was discovered

aptadir-therapeutics-2026.team_highlights: Beyond CEO Giovanni Amabile (Enthera, ADIENNE), the team includes Vittorio de Franciscis, professor at CNR (Italy's National Research Council), Marcin Kortylewski, professor at City of Hope, and other world-leading RNA and epigenetics scientists.

product.summary: An RNA therapeutic based on the DiRs (DNMTs Interacting RNAs) platform, which binds the DNMT1 enzyme and selectively suppresses DNA methylation of specific genes at the individual gene level. Lead pipeline is CAP1-FMR1, targeting Fragile X syndrome.
product.problem_statement: FMR1 gene silencing causes FMRP protein deficiency, leading to intellectual disability and developmental delay. Existing demethylating agents (e.g., azacitidine) nonspecifically suppress the entire genome, resulting in high toxicity and short duration of action.
key_features: Selective DNMT1 inhibition at the single-gene level (locus-specific demethylation)
No cytotoxicity; improved safety profile versus existing drugs
Based on short RNA oligonucleotides, potentially eliminating the need for separate delivery vehicles such as LNPs
product.tech_stack_or_innovation: The DiR (DNMTs Interacting RNAs) mechanism stems from a foundational discovery published in Nature in 2014. It combines RNA aptamer technology with epigenetic editing, and unlike existing CRISPR/dCas9-based epigenome editing, it can be approached by simple RNA oligonucleotide injection.
product.target_customer: Approximately 1 million Fragile X syndrome patients worldwide and their families. Longer term, patients with more than 15 intractable genetic diseases and cancers, including Myelodysplastic Syndrome (MDS).
product.business_model: After developing drugs, will conduct its own clinical trials and pursue technology transfer/co-development. Strategy includes securing FDA Fast Track and PRV (Priority Review Voucher) for rare disease programs.
product.solution: DiRs selectively targets only DNMT1 bound to specific gene promoters to reverse methylation, normalizing gene expression without cytotoxicity. It is designed in two modes: aptaDiR (systemic inhibition) and captaDiR (gene-specific).

direct_competitors.name: Existing demethylating agents (Vidaza, Dacogen)
direct_competitors.comparison: Genome-wide nonspecific methylation inhibition causes severe toxicity including bone marrow suppression. Aptadir differentiates with gene-specific DiRs for safety and durability.

direct_competitors.name: RNA therapeutic platforms (Ionis, Arrowhead, Alnylam)
direct_competitors.comparison: They mainly pursue gene silencing strategies. Aptadir works through the opposite mechanism—reactivating silenced genes.

competitive_landscape.key_differentiator: The only RNA platform achieving gene-level demethylation targeting Fragile X syndrome. Unlike existing epigenome-editing technologies (CRISPR-dCas9, etc.), it can be delivered by simple RNA oligo injection without the complexity of a separate delivery vehicle.
competitive_landscape.competitive_position_summary: Virtually unique position as an RNA demethylation therapeutic targeting Fragile X syndrome. No direct competition from existing non-specific anticancer chemotherapy or gene-silencing RNA therapeutics.
competitive_landscape.moat: More than a decade of patents and IP ahead of the DiRs discovery published in Nature in 2014. Exclusive licenses from Harvard Medical School, Italy's CNR, and Singapore's CSI. Financial firepower secured through Europe's largest-ever seed round, led by 4BIO Capital.

nexosai-2026.tagline: Enterprise AI gateway and workspace that controls 200+ models from a single layer

founders.background: Co-founder of Lithuanian venture group Tesonet. Together with Eimantas Sabaliauskas, he bootstrapped Nord Security (operator of NordVPN) for 12 years into a unicorn; Oxylabs, Hostinger and others also came out of the Tesonet ecosystem.
founders.notable_achievement: Founder who grew Nord Security to a $1.6B valuation in 2022 and later $3B. nexos.ai is his second big challenge; it came out of stealth in January 2025 and secured Index Ventures' first Lithuanian investment.

founders.background: Co-founder of Nord Security and partner at Tesonet. Has experience distributing cybersecurity products to global B2C/B2B markets.
founders.notable_achievement: Co-founder who established the NordVPN brand in global markets. At nexos.ai, he serves as founder and board member.

nexosai-2026.team_highlights: The team's core asset is that both founders are security entrepreneurs who built Nord Security. Per the public leadership page, Emanuelis Norbutas (CTO), Justas Morkūnas (COO), Mykolas Dumčius (CPO) and Gediminas Lisauskas (head of engineering) split product and operations, and much of the organization appears to have been recruited from the Tesonet ecosystem network. Total headcount has not been officially confirmed.

product.summary: nexos.ai pairs a developer-facing AI gateway with an employee-facing AI workspace, letting enterprises use 200+ LLMs under a single policy, cost, and logging layer. The platform and most models are hosted in Europe.
product.problem_statement: Shadow AI — employees uploading financial statements, legal documents, and strategic materials into unauthorized consumer AI tools — is spreading out of control. At the same time, each department manages different model API keys and subscriptions, costs are fragmented, and security teams cannot later verify which model processed what data. The founder describes it as 'security teams chasing ransomware while employees commit the biggest data leak in company history.'
product.solution: It routes all AI traffic through a single gateway, centrally controlling model selection, policy and spend, and gives employees a secure chat/agent interface that only exposes approved models. All interactions on both surfaces remain auditable logs that can be exported to the enterprise's SIEM and identity management systems.
key_features: AI Gateway: orchestrates 200+ models through a single API endpoint with smart routing, caching, and context compression.
Failure handling: automatic fallback and load balancing when a specific provider goes down or hits rate limits.
RAG: retrieval-augmented generation that grounds responses in internal documents.
AI Workspace: compare and chat with multiple LLMs on one screen, handle all file formats, and reuse prompts and agent workflows.
Integrations: connects to Slack, Jira, Confluence, and GitHub to tie into existing work context.
Governance: model access control (RBAC) by user and application, budget and usage limits, role-based permissions.
Observability: logs and traces every request, visibility into org-wide spend, and log export to security systems.
Data protection: zero data retention option, private model hosting for sensitive data, and hosting within Europe.
product.tech_stack_or_innovation: The innovation is not in the models but in the 'control point.' It consolidates the per-provider API keys, rate limits, and fallback logic that teams used to manage individually into a single gateway, and layers an employee UI on top so security policies apply to both humans and code simultaneously. No separately confirmed public materials on the tech stack are available.
product.target_customer: Mid-to-large enterprises with separate security, IT, and finance organizations and regulated AI usage. Especially regulated industries with European data sovereignty requirements. Nord Security is disclosed as a reference customer.
product.business_model: Subscription SaaS appears to be the base model, but the exact combination of workspace seat pricing and gateway usage-based pricing is not confirmed by public materials (est.).

direct_competitors.comparison: A developer-focused LLM gateway and observability tool. nexos.ai treats it as occupying the same layer, even publishing direct comparison content on its own blog. The difference is that nexos.ai also offers a workspace for non-developer employees and an organization-level governance UI.

It has a strong model routing and marketplace character, with fast penetration among individual developers and startups. However, enterprise approval workflows, audit logs, and employee-facing interfaces are nexos.ai's territory.

An open-source proxy that is free and self-hostable, it creates a price resistance line. nexos.ai sells hosting, governance, and support, and must keep proving its value gap versus open-source alternatives.

direct_competitors.name: Cloudflare AI Gateway / infrastructure providers such as AWS and Kong
direct_competitors.comparison: Sells gateway features bundled into already-contracted cloud and edge infrastructure. As standalone features they are close to free, so nexos.ai must hold its ground with the bundle value of 'workspace + policy + European hosting.'

direct_competitors.name: Glean, ChatGPT Enterprise, and other enterprise AI search/assistants
direct_competitors.comparison: They overlap at the employee touchpoint (workspace). The difference is that nexos.ai puts model neutrality, multi-vendor routing, and cost control at the forefront.

competitive_landscape.key_differentiator: A bundle that ties the gateway (developers) and workspace (employees) under the same policy engine, plus a data-sovereignty positioning that puts European hosting and zero data retention front and center.
competitive_landscape.moat: The technology itself is weakly defensible. The real defenses are: 1) early references and trust from the Tesonet ecosystem, including Nord Security; 2) operating experience in implementing the audit, logging, and policy requirements security teams demand deeply into the product; 3) a hosting and compliance position suited to the European regulatory environment. All are the kind that can be caught up over time.
competitive_landscape.competitive_position_summary: The category itself is not yet standardized, and the company sits in a canyon: cloud providers add features for free above, while open source presses prices down below. At the Series A stage, the contest will ultimately turn on whether enterprise security teams approve the budget.

product.problem_statement: Satellite manufacturers face supply bottlenecks due to the high unit cost of space solar cells and long lead times (more than one year after ordering). product.solution: Flexell adopts a tandem structure that stacks CIGS, a thin-film solar material used in terrestrial applications, as the bottom cell, and perovskite, a next-generation high-efficiency material, as the top cell. This substantially lowers manufacturing cost (around KRW 10K per unit) and reduces weight and volume by building the cells on flexible substrates. By using inorganic perovskite instead of organic perovskite, which is vulnerable to temperature changes, the company aims to ensure reliability under the extreme temperatures and radiation of space.

One-fifth to one-tenth the weight, with a rollable design that can be rolled into a cylinder

Acquiring real orbital data, including launches on the Nuri rocket's 4th and 5th missions and a six-month ISS demonstration

product.summary: Manastu develops MS-289, a proprietary hydrogen-peroxide-alcohol-based propellant, and a green-propellant thruster and propulsion module lineup spanning 5 mN to 300 N thrust classes, and plans to combine it with orbital collision-avoidance, maneuvering, end-of-life de-orbit services, and satellite-to-satellite in-orbit refueling technology.
product.problem_statement: Satellite propulsion systems still mostly use toxic, carcinogenic propellants such as hydrazine. Ground handling requires protective gear and dedicated facilities, and launch-site integration procedures are complex, creating major cost and schedule burdens. At the same time, the growing number of small satellites has increased orbital congestion and collision risk, making the ability to conduct collision-avoidance maneuvers or de-orbit after end of life effectively a requirement.
product.solution: The company develops a green propulsion system that combines MS-289 (a self-developed hydrogen-peroxide-alcohol propellant with additives), an ultra-high-temperature ceramic catalyst, and an integrated engine system. The company claims the propellant offers 50% higher performance than hydrazine and is safer to handle. The propulsion system is designed to scale from a 2U small satellite module to a 300 N-class system for launch vehicle upper stages and orbital transfer vehicles (OTVs).
key_features: Vyom 2U: 2U plug-and-play green propulsion system, TRL 8 (orbit-demonstrated), for 6U-24U+ satellites, 1,600 N·s class
I-Booster: for 100-500 kg satellites, 4 × 1 N thrust, 14,000-20,000 N·s, TRL 7
Sharanga: 1-10 mN micro propulsion system, for 3U-10U+ CubeSats, 400 N·s, TRL 7
GP-LAM: 300 N-class thruster for LEO circularization, GTO-GEO transfer, orbit correction, and collision avoidance on launch vehicle upper stages, OTVs, and micro-GEO satellites
Mission design and systems integration engineering services including collision-avoidance maneuvers, orbit changes, and end-of-life de-orbit
Developing satellite in-orbit refueling technology as a separate track
product.tech_stack_or_innovation: The core is the self-developed MS-289 propellant combined with a matching ultra-high-temperature ceramic catalyst and engine. According to the company, the propellant targets handling safety at a level 'safer than common salt,' while improving propulsive performance and ground operational convenience over hydrazine-based systems. The differentiator is an expandable architecture that reuses modules across thrust classes, letting the same fuel and catalyst family cover everything from CubeSats to launch vehicle upper stages.
product.target_customer: Small satellite operators (6U-500 kg), developers of launch vehicle upper stages, OTVs, and landers, micro-GEO satellite operators, university and research institute CubeSat programs, and satellite operators that need orbital collision-avoidance and de-orbit capability.
product.business_model: Sales of propulsion hardware (thrusters and propulsion modules) and propellant, engineering services such as mission design and systems integration, and government R&D contracts are the current pillars. The plan is to add recurring revenue from in-orbit servicing such as orbital refueling and de-orbit in the future. Product pricing and revenue mix have not been disclosed.

spiko-2026.tagline: A fintech that turns cash into yield through tokenized money market funds

founders.background: Graduated from École Polytechnique. Pre-founding career is not widely known, but he worked at the intersection of finance and technology.
École Polytechnique graduate and applied mathematician. Led a technical team at Palantir, then served as an advisor on digital transformation to the French government.
founders.notable_achievement: Advisor on digital transformation to the French government

spiko-2026.team_highlights: Both co-founders are École Polytechnique alumni; Antoine Michon led a technical team at Palantir and served as an advisor on digital transformation to the French government.

product.summary: A platform that generates yield by investing companies' and individuals' idle cash in a blockchain-based tokenized money market fund (MMF). Anyone can access it easily via web/app and API, and redeem in real time.
product.problem_statement: The approx. $50T in cash held by companies and individuals is locked in bank deposits and earns almost nothing. Money market funds are hard to access, and procedures such as opening a traditional securities account are complex.
product.solution: Fund shares are tokenized and recorded on the blockchain, enabling instant sign-up and redemption without a traditional securities account. It can be embedded into corporate treasury systems (TMS) via API, and AI agents can execute automated management rules.
key_features: Instant sign-up and redemption via web/mobile app
Multi-currency funds including euro, dollar, pound and Swiss franc
24/7 operation with blockchain records (including weekends and holidays)
Integration with corporate treasury systems via REST API
Automated withdrawal rules (payroll, supplier payments, etc.)
product.tech_stack_or_innovation: Fund management is outsourced to asset managers such as Amundi, with custody handled by CACEIS of Crédit Agricole. Fund shares are recorded on the same blockchain as stablecoins, turning them into programmable assets.
product.target_customer: Any organization with surplus cash, including SMEs, startups, research institutes, public institutions, VCs and individual investors
product.business_model: Charges only management fees, with no separate platform fee. Quoted yields are transparently disclosed as net returns after fees.

direct_competitors.comparison: A vertically integrated asset manager running its own funds, but its distribution channels are traditional and it is expanding with a crypto focus. Spiko is stronger in non-crypto channels.
Spiko is assessed as having the more diverse tokenized fund lineup (per RWA.xyz).

direct_competitors.name: Banks' in-house MMF products
direct_competitors.comparison: Cumbersome procedures and restricted redemptions put it behind Spiko on UX.

competitive_landscape.key_differentiator: A user experience that skips traditional securities account procedures through tokenization, enabling instant redemption and 24/7 operation. It also secures new distribution channels via API and embedded finance.
competitive_landscape.moat: Product UX and embedded distribution channels. Traditional asset managers are locked into existing distribution channels and struggle to expand into new ones (fintechs, TMS, AI agents).
competitive_landscape.competitive_position_summary: The market is still early, but with $2.7B in AUM and 5x annual growth, it is rapidly expanding its position in the B2B segment.

trending_reason.summary: Raised a $90M Series B led by NEA in October 2026 (valuation $800M). AUM grew 5x in a year to $2.7B, and it is expanding across Europe.

AUM grew 5x in a year to $2.7B
Participation from major VCs including NEA, Index Ventures and Bpifrance
Expansion beyond France and the UK into Germany, the Nordics, Italy, Spain and other European markets
trending_reason.growth_metrics: AUM $2.7B (5x increase from a year earlier), 10,000+ customers, presence in 25+ countries

Led by Index Ventures. Exact date not disclosed.

market_outlook.market_trend: Growing demand for tokenized real-world assets (RWA) and programmable finance. With policy rates at 2.5–4%, demand for yield on deposits is expanding.
market_outlook.growth_potential: AUM is negligible relative to TAM, but given 5x annual growth, major growth is possible in a short period.
risks: Potential changes to securities laws and AML regulations in each country
Intensifying competition from traditional banks and asset managers
Technology risk from reliance on blockchain and smart contracts
Delayed adoption due to the conservative stance of corporate treasury teams
market_outlook.risk_mitigation: Prioritizes regulatory compliance and works with French regulators. Secures credibility by using a bank (Crédit Agricole) as custodian. Also compatible with traditional infrastructure beyond blockchain.

mural-2026.tagline: Global financial infrastructure for fintech and AI agents

product.summary: Mural is a compliant system of record that provides fintechs and platforms with accounts, payments, identity verification, and regulatory compliance infrastructure spanning traditional banking networks and stablecoin payment rails through a single API.
product.problem_statement: Global businesses must separately connect to multiple banks, payment providers, and compliance vendors, and this integration is slow, costly, and difficult to maintain. With the emergence of AI agents, direct access to bank accounts is also restricted.
product.solution: Mural lets customers manage fiat currency and stablecoins in one place and launch financial products quickly through built-in compliance features and forward-deployed engineering support. It can also provide dedicated wallets for AI agents with spending policies.
key_features: Mural Accounts: Provides named virtual accounts, custody of USD/EUR/MXN/BRL/ARS/COP fiat currencies and stablecoins
Send: Stablecoin and local fiat payouts (around 20 currencies in total, including USD, EUR, MXN, BRL, ARS, COP, CLP, and PEN)
Compliance built-in: Licensed money transmitter, transaction limits and approval controls, audit trail
Forward-deployed engineers: The team works alongside the customer until they go live
AI agent support: Spending limits, approved counterparties, and additional approval requirements for large payments can be applied to accounts
API-based: All functions, including account creation, KYC, payments, and FX, are integrated into a single API
product.tech_stack_or_innovation: A payments layer that orchestrates stablecoins and local fiat currencies; a system with compliance built in by default; wallet and policy features designed for AI agents
product.target_customer: Companies and platforms seeking to build their own financial products, including fintechs, payroll platforms (Deel), and browser developers (Opera)
product.business_model: Estimated to be transaction fees or a SaaS subscription; not officially disclosed

direct_competitors.comparison: Stripe specializes in payment processing, but Mural provides accounts, compliance, and multi-currency capabilities in a single system, differentiating itself especially in stablecoin and AI agent support.
Wise is strong in money transfers, but Mural provides infrastructure (virtual accounts, compliance) that lets businesses build their own financial products and also includes stablecoin rails.
Circle focuses on USDC issuance and blockchain payments, but Mural manages fiat currency and stablecoins together and handles compliance itself.
Unit provides banking-as-a-service in the United States, but Mural differs in its global (128 countries) multi-currency and stablecoin support.

competitive_landscape.key_differentiator: A single compliant system connecting traditional banking networks and blockchain payment rails simultaneously; a forward-deployed model; built-in dedicated wallet and policy features for AI agents
competitive_landscape.moat: Its own licenses and compliance capabilities; strategic partnership with Tether; track record of processing over $2.1B in payments across 128 countries; large enterprise customers (Deel, Opera)
competitive_landscape.competitive_position_summary: Mural is establishing itself as leading infrastructure in the emerging fields of stablecoins and AI agent finance, and Tether's investment and rapidly growing payment volume attest to its credibility.

trending_reason.summary: In October 2026, it announced a $15M Series A led by Tether, drawing attention as payment infrastructure targeting the AI agent economy. In the same month, it changed its brand from 'Mural Pay' to 'Mural,' and annual payment volume grew 6x, showing rapid expansion.
catalysts: Tether's investment: Stablecoin issuer Tether participated as lead investor, betting on the future of AI agent payments
AI agent market growth: As major banks restrict external AI agents' access to customer accounts, demand for dedicated agent wallets is increasing
Stablecoin payments surge: Real-economy stablecoin payment volume roughly doubled to about $390B in 2025 (McKinsey/Artemis)
Major customer wins: Large platforms such as Deel and Opera use Mural
trending_reason.growth_metrics: Has processed a total of $2.1B in payments since launching its API in 2025; operates in 128 countries; 2026 payment volume is about 6x that of all of 2025

funding.total_raised_note: Includes the $15M Series A, a $5M Seed round, and additional funding such as pre-seed

funding_history.note: Seed round in 2022 according to Fortune article

market_outlook.tam_sam_som: TAM: Global cross-border payments market (multi-trillion-dollar scale) and stablecoin payments market (approx. $390B in 2025); SAM: Global accounts and payments infrastructure for fintechs and platforms; SOM: Target of tens of billions of dollars annually from the current $2.1B in payment volume
market_outlook.market_trend: Accelerating real-economy adoption of stablecoins; growing demand for compliant agent wallets as AI agents emerge as economic actors; deepening multi-currency and compliance complexity as companies expand globally
market_outlook.growth_potential: If the AI agent payments market takes off in earnest, Mural's infrastructure is highly likely to become an essential adoption. It has already secured large customers such as Deel and Opera and is growing rapidly with annual payment volume up 6x
risks: Regulatory risk: Changes in financial regulation across countries and uncertainty around stablecoin regulation
Intensifying competition: Large companies such as Stripe and Circle may launch similar features
Tether dependence: Risks associated with Tether, a major investor and partner (regulatory issues, reserve controversies), pose indirect risks
Technology dependence: Stability of and reliance on stablecoins and blockchain networks
market_outlook.risk_mitigation: Expanding its own license portfolio and complying with regulations across multiple jurisdictions; mitigating reliance on a single technology by providing both fiat rails and stablecoin rails; diversifying customers (fintech, payroll, browser, etc.)

trajectory-2026.tagline: A platform for domain experts to directly post-train AI models.

founders.background: One of three Stanford classmates. Researched at Google DeepMind, and was one of the researchers who joined when DeepMind acqui-hired Windsurf talent.
founders.notable_achievement: As a DeepMind acqui-hire, raised $45M Series A led by Sequoia within a year of founding.

founders.background: Stanford classmate. Former Google DeepMind. Publicly emphasizes safety of learning methods that maintain human intervention over autonomous self-improvement (RSI).
founders.notable_achievement: Led design of post-training pipeline based on DeepMind research experience (Crunchbase misspells last name as 'Elab').

founders.background: Stanford classmate. Researched generative foundation models at Apple. Currently leads interface design for non-technical users of the product.
founders.notable_achievement: Transformed Apple generative model research experience into product UX, implemented interface enabling 'learning without researchers.'

trajectory-2026.team_highlights: 18 people in the first year of founding. All three founders are Stanford classmates from Google DeepMind and Apple, and have recruited researchers and product designers from OpenAI, Stripe, and Netflix. The emphasis on designer headcount is because the competitive edge lies in 'whether non-technical experts can use it,' not model performance.

product.summary: A self-service platform that collects real usage signals like traces, corrections, and re-prompts from a company's own products, and continuously post-trains open-source models for the domain. Officially launched on November 2, 2026.
product.problem_statement: General-purpose foundation models cannot self-correct repeated mistakes in specific domains. To address this, companies had to build in-house research teams or hire expensive forward-deployed engineers (FDEs), and in areas like law and finance where correct answers depend on expert judgment, creating evaluation criteria itself was difficult.
product.solution: Connect with two lines of code to the agent execution environment (harness), and when customers provide examples of 'what is a good result,' it handles training, evaluation, comparison, and deployment in one screen. All updates must pass the customer's evaluation suite and approval workflow before being reflected in production.
key_features: Bring your own agents: Integrate with any agent harness, start by modifying two code locations.
One-click training, one-click deployment: No need to directly manage sandbox, orchestration, or infrastructure.
Continual Grading (research preview): Learn from a few expert-graded scoring examples to extend criteria across operational data.
Group Size 1 (research preview): Train on actual production interaction units to improve the model even after launch.
Comparison view with frontier models: See where and why your own model outperforms.
Data governance: Customers specify data boundaries, with full audit logs and visibility for training runs.
SOC 2 certification (as self-reported by the company).
product.tech_stack_or_innovation: The core is a continual learning loop based on open-source models. The SDK collects modification, correction, and re-prompt signals, and post-training cycles run weekly or more frequently per company materials. However, it is more of a phased pipeline of collect-train-evaluate-approve-deploy rather than an 'every interaction instantly changes the model' approach. Continual Grading and Group Size 1 are still research previews.
product.target_customer: AI-native companies operating their own AI products and domain-specific professional SaaS. Legal AI Harvey, financial AI Rogo, talent matching Mercor, and Nvidia were mentioned as customers. End users are practicing professionals like lawyers, doctors, and analysts, not researchers.
product.business_model: Assumed to be platform subscription SaaS, but pricing and unit costs not confirmed in public materials (est.).

direct_competitors.comparison: Fine-tuning API from the company founded by Mira Murati. Manages distributed training on its own cluster and shares compute via LoRA to lower costs. Removed the waitlist in December 2025. While its strength is infrastructure management, Trajectory focuses on domain expert judgment input and approval workflows.
A fine-tuning platform reported to be valued at $3.25B in October 2026. Ahead of Trajectory ($300M) in funding and infrastructure scale.
A platform for companies to build and train their own agents. While it covers agent training broadly, Trajectory is narrowly focused on 'post-training for production agents already in operation.'

direct_competitors.name: Foundation labs' own features (OpenAI, Anthropic fine-tuning APIs)
direct_competitors.comparison: If general-purpose model providers offer training features by default, the reason to use a separate vendor diminishes. Trajectory counters this threat with open-source models and customer-owned evaluation criteria.

competitive_landscape.key_differentiator: Practicing professionals, not researchers, directly define evaluation criteria and run training. The team composition, which has placed interface design as a core competency from the early days of founding, supports this.
competitive_landscape.moat: The evaluation criteria, scoring examples, and trace data accumulated at customer sites act as de facto switching costs. However, with an 18-person organization in its first year and some core features in research preview, the current moat is at the level of the team and initial references (Harvey, Rogo, Mercor, Nvidia).
competitive_landscape.competitive_position_summary: The market is already flush with capital. Trajectory differentiates on the axis of 'domain experts become the owners of the training loop' rather than 'managing infrastructure for you,' but there are multiple competitors who can push the same argument with larger capital.

This was a consecutive round about six months after coming out of stealth in May 2026 and about five months after the seed round.

founders.notable_achievement: Co-founded Blacksmith in 2024. Prior experience in large-scale distributed systems and search infrastructure.

blacksmith-2026.team_highlights: Y Combinator alumni. Approximately 30 people as of August 2026. Cockroach Labs CEO Spencer Kimball participates as an angel investor. Hiring in New York and San Francisco.

product.summary: A CI-dedicated infrastructure platform for verifying large-scale code changes generated by AI coding agents before merging. Provides a drop-in runner that can be switched with a one-line change to a GitHub Actions workflow.
product.problem_statement: As AI coding agents dramatically accelerate code writing, 'code verification' is emerging as the new bottleneck. Developers' PR counts have increased several times to dozens of times, but existing general-purpose cloud CI cannot efficiently handle spike workloads. Anthropic reports that its own CI volume increased 25x in 6 months.
product.solution: Operates a CI-dedicated hardware-software stack based on bare-metal gaming CPUs in its own data centers. Absorbs CI workloads that vary from 0 to tens of thousands of CPUs for a single customer, delivering on average 2x faster build completion and 60% cost reduction.
key_features: GitHub Actions runner: Bare-metal gaming CPUs, Linux/macOS/Windows, x64/ARM, 2-32 vCPUs, instant provisioning, unlimited concurrency
Observability Console: execution history, global log search, test analysis, CI analytics, SSH debug
CI Caching: co-located dependency cache, NVMe Docker layer cache, sticky disk, git checkout snapshots
[code]smith: a cloud coding agent that operates within the team's CI environment
Proof: a private beta feature that runs PR code to prove that changes work as claimed
product.tech_stack_or_innovation: Bare-metal hardware stack designed exclusively for CI. Operates approximately 10MW of computing in US and Europe data centers. Customers do not need infrastructure provisioning, scaling, or maintenance.
product.target_customer: Startups and enterprise development organizations that have actively adopted AI coding agents. Over 10,000 companies including Mercury, Granola, Handshake, LangChain, Ashby, etc.
product.business_model: Usage-based pricing (CI job execution volume). Controls costs through own hardware operations and offers prices on average 60% lower than GitHub Actions.

direct_competitors.comparison: The default CI choice for developers. Inefficient for spike workloads due to general-purpose VMs. Blacksmith claims 2x faster performance and 60% lower cost with a drop-in replacement.
AI labs aiming to integrate code verification into their AI agents. Strength is vertical integration of code generation and verification.
An AI agent whose own CI volume increased 25x in 6 months. A potential competitor that could internalize verification infrastructure.

AI computing platform. Raised $750M on 2026-10-14 ($15.75B valuation). An adjacent competitor with significantly larger capital resources.

product.summary: An agentic service management platform that deploys AI agents ('AI Coworker') across enterprise IT, HR, finance, and legal service tasks, and manages agent-specific roles, budgets, permissions, and audit trails.
product.problem_statement: Legacy ITSM like ServiceNow takes a long time to set up and its structure is outdated for humans and agents to use together in the AI era. Moreover, simple chatbot-level AI cannot handle real ticket resolution or account provisioning, and there is a lack of controls to govern and audit agents.
product.solution: Receives employee requests via work messengers like Slack and Teams, and AI agents resolve them directly. It layers on top of existing systems like ServiceNow or Jira Service Management, so it can be adopted without migration. All agent actions are recorded in audit logs.
key_features: Atom: A universal AI coworker that works via chat, voice, and vision across Teams, Slack, MCP clients, email, browser, and portal
Assign roles, skills, budgets, and access permissions per AI agent
Audit trail for all agent activities
Integration with existing ITSM like ServiceNow, Jira Service Management
Automate workflows for IT, HR, finance, legal, and workplace
Security options for enterprises to bring their own model endpoints or retain encryption keys
product.tech_stack_or_innovation: Built on Microsoft Azure AI Foundry, supports MCP (Model Context Protocol) clients. Allows BYOK and custom LLM endpoint configuration to ensure enterprise data control.
product.target_customer: Global enterprises with annual revenue of approx. $1B+ and 1,000+ employees. Known customers include Zuora, Pepper Money, and Ammex Corporation, primarily in the US.
product.business_model: Estimated to be a cloud SaaS subscription model, likely usage and license-based billing for AI agents. Specific pricing is not disclosed.

direct_competitors.comparison: Incumbent standard in the ITSM market. It is strengthening AI agent orchestration capabilities but legacy architecture and long implementation times are cited as weaknesses.
Strengths in conversational AI-based employee support automation. Atomicwork adds 'AI workforce' governance that manages budgets, permissions, and audits.

product.summary: Orbis is a video foundation model that 'runs' in real time rather than 'rendering' a finished clip. It streams at 4K resolution and 24fps; if the prompt is changed during generation, the scene updates immediately without starting over. product.problem_statement: Existing generative video is offline: input a prompt, wait, and receive a finished output, so modifying a result requires regenerating the entire clip, and there is no continuity or interactivity. product.solution: A real-time streaming generator plus streaming upscaler architecture, with a latent world model that evaluates candidate future scenes at inference time to induce physically plausible motion. The technical report says real-time performance was achieved through distillation—transferring the performance of a large model into a smaller one.

Changing the prompt mid-generation updates the scene immediately without restarting
Hierarchical memory that preserves characters, backgrounds, and art style at the scene level
Generation grounded in physical dynamics (latent world model)

competitive_landscape.key_differentiator: While most generative video is offline rendering, Orbis continues running instead of finishing, allowing user intervention midstream. The company's central claim is maintaining real-time 4K at 24fps—for hours—without quality degradation.
competitive_landscape.moat: Latent-world-model-grounded physical dynamics, a chunk-based streaming and distillation pipeline, and know-how in optimizing real-time inference on TPU environments. competitive_landscape.competitive_position_summary: In the world-model camp, Visko is a challenger betting on duration and consistency within the resolution–duration–interactivity triangle. It has secured a technical demo and infrastructure partnerships, but without disclosed commercial customers, pricing, or revenue, it remains in the proof-of-technology stage.

navanaai-2026.tagline: Enterprise voice AI platform supporting 12 Indian languages and 45 dialects

founders.background: Second-time founder. Previously founded a mobile game studio and, together with his brother Jai, founded Navana.ai in 2018, leading the strategy to build speech recognition, synthesis, and language models all in-house.
founders.notable_achievement: CEO who secured major Indian BFSI customers including Bajaj Finserv, Ujjivan, and Jana Small Finance Bank and achieved over 100M minutes of voice AI processing.

founders.background: Software engineer who studied computer engineering at the University of Michigan. Co-founded the company with his brother Raoul and designed the 'Bodhi' stack composed of proprietary ASR, TTS, and language models.
founders.notable_achievement: Technical leader who designed models about 5x smaller than competing architectures, enabling voice AI to run inside bank data centers.

navanaai-2026.team_highlights: A small organization of 37 employees per PitchBook. The founder brothers serve as CEO and CTO, and it has voice AI research talent that jointly built the RESPIN open speech dataset (9 languages, 38 dialects, 10K+ hours) with IISc Bangalore.

product.summary: Full-stack voice AI platform for Indian BFSI enterprises. Based on its proprietary Bodhi model family (ASR, TTS, language models), it provides phone voice agents, real-time transcription and summarization, and call analytics APIs, deployed on-premises in customer data centers.
product.problem_statement: Global voice AI is trained mainly on English and Hindi and cannot accurately handle Indians' code-mixing (e.g., Marathi-to-Hindi switching), dialects, noise, and fast speech. In financial and insurance consultations, misrecognizing a single word can lead to loan errors, missed insurance claims, and regulatory violations.
product.solution: A 'sovereign AI' architecture that deploys proprietary Bodhi models trained on over 50K hours of real Indian calls to customers' private clouds. It provides AI contact center, voice API, and audio intelligence as a single stack, solving accuracy and compliance simultaneously.
key_features: Supports 12 Indian languages and 45 dialects (Hindi, Telugu, Tamil, Marathi, Bengali, Odia, Malayalam, Kannada, Gujarati, English, etc.)
On-premises deployment-only architecture — customer voice and personal data do not go to third-party model providers
AI contact center platform: build, operate, and automatically evaluate phone voice agents
Audio intelligence API: batch transcription, call summarization, consultation performance insights
Bodhi TTS: 10 languages, 50+ native voices, ₹12 per 100K characters (approx. ₹0.72 per minute)
product.tech_stack_or_innovation: Owns speech recognition (ASR), speech synthesis (TTS), and language models all developed in-house. Models about 5x smaller than competitors can run in bank data centers. Jointly built the 'RESPIN' open dataset (9 languages, 38 dialects, 10K+ hours) with IISc Bangalore. ISO 27001, SOC 2 Type II, RBI guideline compliant.
product.target_customer: Large Indian BFSI companies. Current customers include Bajaj Finserv, Protean, Ujjivan Small Finance Bank, Jana Small Finance Bank, and Grihum Housing Finance.
product.business_model: Per-minute usage billing for calls + on-premises deployment and tuning revenue. TTS is a separate API at ₹12 per 100K characters. Also transfers capabilities so customer internal teams can operate their own AI contact centers.

direct_competitors.comparison: An Indian voice AI startup that raised $13M in the same period. A cloud-based general-purpose voice AI platform targeting finance, healthcare, contact centers, and BPO. Navana specializes in on-premises deployment and BFSI regulatory response.

competitive_landscape.moat: Proprietary data from over 50K hours of real Indian calls, a learning loop reinvested through 100M+ minutes processed cumulatively in BFSI, compliance meeting RBI data localization regulations, and references from large BFSI customers.
